need: Local StarCi FE, API, and identity services must have one Control-Panel-delegated runtime-owner task. Every feature, audit, quality, and UAT task consumes the same localhost:3000, localhost:3001, and localhost:8080 runtime and communicates health or recovery needs to that owner instead of claiming ports, replacing processes, or rebinding server environment for its UAT account.
negativeBoundary: Do not serialize all feature work merely because the runtime is shared, centralize feature source ownership, store credentials in the runtime registry, let the runtime task mutate product source, or treat a listening port alone as a ready receipt. Account and fixture isolation remain per UAT run and Browser session.
acceptanceCriteria: Runtime configuration declares centralized-task ownership, Control Panel authority, canonical localhost endpoints, a local-only owner registry, and forbidden feature-task process mutation.
A schema-validated local registry identifies exactly one owner thread generation, state, canonical endpoints, health evidence, and update time without credentials.
Frontend and UAT guidance forbid feature tasks from starting, stopping, restarting, replacing, killing, or claiming shared listeners and route recovery requests to the registered runtime owner.
UAT account isolation uses account and Browser-session boundaries against the shared runtime rather than per-feature API processes or server-environment rebinding.
Executable regression coverage rejects non-localhost registry endpoints and incomplete owner identity while accepting the canonical centralized runtime contract.

accepts: Use one dedicated runtime task created by the Control Panel for FE 3000, API 3001, and identity 8080.
Make every feature task communicate runtime needs to that task while continuing to isolate its own UAT account and Browser session.
Keep shared runtime lifecycle separate from feature source, audit, and business ownership.
rejects: Treat Community, Playground, Dashboard, or another feature task as owner of localhost:3001.
Pause or replace another feature because each task assumes it needs a private API process.
Restart shared servers or rewrite server environment merely to switch the active UAT account.

review.rationale: Owner correction and the observed Playground/Community port-conflict pause prove a systemic runtime-ownership gap. Central ownership preserves shared service continuity while allowing isolated feature UAT sessions.
